api_header:
Available robot APIs. Typed signatures below are reference notation, not Python annotations to emit.
Types:
ObjectHandle: opaque identity of a physical block in this trial, not a number or a position.
The input b0 is a block handle; other handles come from selection queries or lambda bindings.
Position3: copied immutable world-frame (X,Y,Z) in metres. Blocks are represented by centres;
the gripper position is the controller's end-effector position. Only literal indices 0,1,2 are allowed.
Offset3: a list/tuple of exactly three finite scalar displacements in metres, not an absolute target.
Scalar: a finite int/float, not a Boolean. Bool: True or False. None: no returned value.
These type names are explanatory; do not import, construct, or inspect them.

api_entries.Pick:
Pick(block: ObjectHandle) -> None
block is the block to grasp. Approach horizontally at the current gripper height, open,
descend to the block centre, and close. No automatic lift or transport follows.
Opening may release a carried block; do not add a Pick inside a movement-only helper.
api_entries.Move:
Move(x_ref: ObjectHandle, y_ref: ObjectHandle, z_ref: ObjectHandle, offset: Offset3) -> None
Exactly FOUR positional arguments. The first three are blocks, never Position3 or scalars.
x_ref supplies world X, y_ref supplies world Y, z_ref supplies world Z; they may differ.
At invocation, sample references once: gripper target =
(X(x_ref)+offset[0], Y(y_ref)+offset[1], Z(z_ref)+offset[2]).
Drive toward this fixed GRIPPER target while commanding the gripper closed.
The target does not track a moving reference during this call. The carried block centre
can differ from the gripper position; account for their measured offset if computing a
block-centre target. Do not assume zero offset or guaranteed rigid attachment.
api_entries.Release:
Release(reference: ObjectHandle, height_offset: Scalar) -> None
reference supplies invocation-time block Z; height_offset is a displacement in metres.
Open at the current location, then retreat to Z(reference at invocation)+height_offset,
preserving pre-opening gripper XY. This does not lower/place the block before opening.
The second argument is not an absolute world Z.
api_entries.get_gripper_position:
get_gripper_position() -> Position3
Read the current gripper XYZ. The getter does not step physics.
api_entries.get_block_position:
get_block_position(block: ObjectHandle) -> Position3
Read this block's current centre XYZ without stepping physics. Saved positions do not
update; read again after motion. A returned Position3 cannot replace a handle.
api_entries.eq:
eq(a: ObjectHandle, b: ObjectHandle) -> Bool
Object identity, not coordinate equality. Handle == and != also compare identity.
api_entries.ON_star:
ON_star(a: ObjectHandle, b: ObjectHandle) -> Bool
True iff abs(X(a)-X(b)) < 0.025 AND abs(Y(a)-Y(b)) < 0.025 AND Z(a) >= Z(b).
Reflexive. Horizontal alignment and relative height alone do not certify physical support.
The formula is mathematical notation; abs is not an available builtin API.
api_entries.ON:
ON(a: ObjectHandle, b: ObjectHandle) -> Bool
True iff a and b are distinct, ON_star(a,b), and no distinct intermediate block c has
both ON_star(a,c) and ON_star(c,b). Irreflexive; not a contact or grasp certificate.
api_entries.Higher:
Higher(a: ObjectHandle, b: ObjectHandle) -> Bool
True iff Z(a) >= Z(b) - {higher_tolerance} metres (the resolved Higher tolerance).
Non-strict and reflexive. This tolerance is separate from controller position tolerance.
api_entries.Scattered:
Scattered(a: ObjectHandle, b: ObjectHandle) -> Bool
True iff abs(X(a)-X(b)) >= 0.10 OR abs(Y(a)-Y(b)) >= 0.10.
This is an axis-separation OR rule, not a Euclidean-distance threshold.
The formula is mathematical notation; abs is not an available builtin API.
api_entries.ON_star_zero:
ON_star_zero(a: ObjectHandle, b: ObjectHandle) -> Bool
ON_star evaluated on frozen trial-entry geometry, not the current positions.
api_entries.exists:
exists(lambda x: condition) -> Bool
True if a physical block binding satisfies the Boolean condition. Multiple lambda
parameters quantify over tuples of blocks; bindings may repeat unless explicitly excluded.
api_entries.forall:
forall(lambda x: condition) -> Bool
True if every physical block binding satisfies the Boolean condition. Multiple lambda
parameters are allowed; bindings may repeat unless explicitly excluded.
api_entries.get:
get(lambda x: condition) -> ObjectHandle
Exactly one lambda parameter. Return the first matching block in host selection order;
raise an execution error if none matches. Never return None, False, a position, or an ID.
When existence is uncertain, guard selection with exists using the same condition.
Query lambdas must return Bool, be action-free, and obey the selected condition mode.

api_footer:
Shared effects and language:
Successful Pick/Move/Release calls return None, not a success Boolean. Controller
nonconvergence raises an execution failure. Each primitive currently has at most 50
simulation steps (Pick's phases share this budget); Move uses a 0.002 m 3D position
tolerance. One simulation step is one env.step(action), not one wall-clock second.
The trial wall-clock cap does not extend primitive limits. Convergence alone does not
certify grasp, collision freedom, physical support, or task completion.
Use assignment, unannotated def/return, if/else, while, break/continue/pass,
Boolean and/or/not, object ==/!=, and finite scalar +,-,*,/ with unary +/-.
Use only positional API calls. Do not redefine the supplied APIs.
Only Position3 literal indexing 0/1/2 is allowed; no general indexing or vector arithmetic.
No imports, attributes, raw observations, images, env/sim access, for loops,
comprehensions, decorators, default/variadic function arguments, dynamic calls, function
aliases, or invented perception APIs.
No builtin math/collection calls are supplied. Lambda expressions are query arguments only.
No table/Goal coordinate handle is exposed. Numbers/positions cannot replace object handles.
Condition helpers and query lambdas must be pure (no physical actions), including callees.
Action helpers must preserve the requested operation's scope and input/return meanings;
a movement-only helper must not add Pick/Release. Prefer direct API composition for small
operations and avoid unnecessary helper layers or self/mutual delegation cycles.
examples:
Interface examples (u,v,w are already bound handles; not safe-path prescriptions):
Valid: Move(u, v, w, [0.01, -0.02, 0.08])
Valid: p = get_block_position(u)  # p is Position3; u remains ObjectHandle
Valid selection pattern:
if exists(lambda x: eq(x, b0)):
    selected = get(lambda x: eq(x, b0))
Invalid arity: Move(u, v, w, 0.0, 0.0, 0.08)
Invalid reference types: Move(p, p, p, [0.0, 0.0, 0.08])
Invalid reference types: Move(p[0], p[1], p[2], [0.0, 0.0, 0.08])
Invalid predicate types: Higher(get_block_position(u), get_block_position(v))
Release(u, p[2]) is type-correct, but wrong if p[2] was intended as an absolute retreat Z.
These fragments illustrate interfaces only; they do not establish a collision-free plan.

condition_rules.dsl_only:
Condition mode: dsl_only.
Loop, branch and selection conditions must use only DSL predicates, object identity,
Boolean logic, quantifiers, and pure helpers composed of those operations.
Position reads and numerical computations may parameterize actions, but numerical
comparisons (including coordinate, counter and constant comparisons) are forbidden.
These rules apply transitively through assignments, helper arguments and returns.
Mathematical predicate formulas above are documentation, not permission to replace DSL calls with numeric conditions.
condition_rules.coordinate_predicates:
Condition mode: coordinate_predicates.
Loop, branch and selection conditions may use DSL predicates, pure numeric predicates,
or Boolean combinations of DSL and/or numeric predicates. Coordinate comparisons,
counters, constants and numeric helper arguments are allowed; numeric provenance is unrestricted.
Numeric <, <=, >, >=, == and != are allowed. Conditions must return Bool and be action-free,
including all helpers they call. Coordinates may also parameterize actions.

output_rules.policy:
Output executable policy code. You may use top-level statements directly.
If you define a policy entry function, invoke it at the top level.
output_rules.helper:
Output only the requested function definition.
Do not include top-level calls or other executable statements outside the function.
The caller is responsible for invoking this helper.
